folder edges align loosely with table rows; last row is cut off at the bottom

collage of photographic objects next to vector UI

collage of objects beside typeset table
t2i_prompt: A 1440 px wide desktop website section, flat straight-on UI mockup on a warm limestone background. Top: a small logo strip, a large light-weight navy sans headline. Left quarter: a top-down photo-real stack of manila, navy and steel-blue file folders cropped at the edge, with paper clips, a binder clip, a small labelled glass vial and a red rubber stamp mark, soft paper shadows and grain. Right three quarters: a calm editorial table with uppercase letter-spaced column headers and hairline row rules, each row holding <CONTENT>. One stamped ink label in a table cell. Warm, archival, precise.
signature_idea: A physical stack of quality-dossier folders becomes the row index of a standards table, so every standard reads as a filed, stamped piece of proof.
strengths: the table itself is clear, legible and content-faithful, which suits spec-reading buyers
folder and stamp metaphor directly says 'documented proof' to QA and validation readers
limestone and navy match the brand palette
light headline and generous row spacing feel calm
weaknesses: photo-real stationery clashes with the brand's line-drawing language and looks like stock imagery
folders do not align with the rows, so the metaphor is decoration, not structure
red stamp adds an unsanctioned accent colour
'STEEL-BLUE' stamp is a leaked prompt word
headline misspelt and last row cut off; no mono figures for codes
brand_fit_why: Limestone and navy with a light headline and calm table are on-brand, but photo-real clutter, a red accent and no mono codes or line drawing move it away from the precise, square, one-accent system.
